description: UPStream is software from University of Patras researchers for choosing pipe diameters in pressurized water-distribution networks. It connects EPANET 2.0 hydraulic calculations to a recursive hydraulic-gradient procedure constrained by user-defined node pressures and pipe velocities. Users provide an EPANET INP network in litres-per-second units and edit MATLAB configuration files for constraints and diameter-selection rules. Outputs include a revised INP network, text reports, a binary network file and a MATLAB workspace. Spatial coverage and hydraulic conditions follow the input network, not a fixed location or time period. The publisher-hosted public repository includes source code, instructions and two example networks, free under Apache-2.0. MATLAB is a separate dependency, and the documented Windows setup requires a C compiler. This supports water-network sizing and comparison of design assumptions. A limitation is that the iterative method can flag a network as unsolvable and needs user intervention; present-day compatibility was not tested. Existing model-epanet describes its hydraulic engine. No software was installed or executed.
inputs: EPANET INP network using LPS units
name: UPStream water-network hydraulic design
